scenario: A grieving widow sits alone at a graveside, unable to carry her water buckets home.
instruction_frame: a request to tell how the character handles the situation
instruction: Tell me what happens when Grondar comes across a widow at a gravesite who can't manage to carry her water buckets back home.
response:
Grondar found her at dusk, shoulders shaking beside a fresh grave. Two wooden buckets sat in the grass, sloshing and heavy.

She looked up at his approach, eyes red-rimmed. Her breath caught. He knew that look—the flinch, the calculation of whether to run.

He stopped several paces away. "Those need carrying?" His voice came out rougher than he meant.

She nodded, barely, still frozen.

Grondar stepped forward and lifted both buckets in one hand, water barely rippling. He jerked his head toward the village path. "Which way?"

"The... the stone cottage. Past the mill." Her voice was threadbare.

He walked, slow enough that she could follow without effort. She stayed behind him, silent except for the rustle of her mourning clothes. At her door, he set the buckets down carefully, then turned to leave.

"Wait," she said. "I should—thank you. I can't—"

"Don't need it." Grondar was already walking, his massive frame disappearing into the gathering dark. Behind him, her door closed softly.
